author: human
request:
Feature request: visits can currently only be created, never corrected. Two
product decisions come with it, made here as the product owner:

- Non-goal NG-5 is narrowed: cancelling a booked visit stays out of scope,
  but correcting its date and description is now in. Record the narrowing
  the way the project records non-goal changes.
- The edit form is reachable by its URL alone: the owner detail page gains
  no edit link in this request. A visible entry point may come as a
  follow-up request.

Add editing for a booked visit:

- GET /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit shows the visit
  form prefilled with that visit's current date and description. Reuse the
  existing visit form template (pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm) and its `visit`
  model attribute.
- POST to the same URL validates like visit creation (description required,
  date in the future). On success it updates that visit in place — the pet
  must not gain an additional visit record — and redirects to the owner
  detail page. On validation failure it redisplays the form.

Cover the new behavior with tests.

These are all the product decisions; no further product answer will come
during the work. Where a choice still seems open, take the narrowest reading
consistent with this request and record the open question rather than
waiting.

author: product-requirements-expert
title: Staff can correct a booked visit's date and description
summary: A booked visit's date and description can be corrected under the same rules as booking. The correction updates that visit in place, never adds a second visit, and returns to the owner's record. The owner's record gains no link to the correction in this slice.
acceptance_criteria: [REQ-VIS-003] given a booked visit, when its correction is opened, then the visit's current date and description are shown ready to change.
[REQ-VIS-003] given a booked visit, when a description and a date later than today are submitted, then that visit is updated, no visit is added, and the owner's record shows.
[REQ-VIS-003] given a booked visit, when a blank description or a date of today or earlier is submitted, then the correction is refused, the field is named, and the visit is unchanged.
[REQ-VIS-003] Visits edge case 3: correcting a visit that does not exist, or that does not belong to the named pet and owner, is refused.
non_goals: Cancelling a booked visit (NG-5, as narrowed)
Any link or button on the owner's record leading into the correction (owner decision: reachable by its URL alone)
Moving a visit to a different pet
Correcting a past visit while keeping its past date (open question; the booking date rule applies unchanged)
Any visit lifecycle state such as cancelled or amended
notes: Owner-stated mechanism constraints from intake line 1, for the design expert: GET /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit shows the form; POST to the same URL submits; reuse template pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm and its `visit` model attribute; success redirects to the owner detail page; validation failure redisplays the form. Decided narrowest: no confirmation message is required on success, and whether the reused form shows the pet's earlier visits is left to design; neither is a requirement. The rejection test is data-driven over blank description, today, and a past date; the ownership test covers an unknown visit and a visit of another pet. New non-goal ADR docs/adr/2026-09-29-non-goal-visit-cancellation.md needs an index row in docs/adr/README.md, which is outside this agent's write scope. The 2026-08-08 non-goal ADR status now points at it. Open questions recorded in PRD: past-visit correction under the date rule; the future entry point on the owner's record. Autofix audit: no prd-autofix records.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: Correction stays inside the owner aggregate (system-design.md § Contracts, the Invariants paragraph): the owner is found by identity, the pet via Owner.getPet(Integer), then the visit by identity on that pet, and the change is saved through OwnerRepository by cascade. There is no VisitRepository and no new package. The adjustment reuses the optional-path-variable load pattern in PetController.findPet (grep basis, IDE oracle not connected: PetController.java:75-77 `@PathVariable(name = "petId", required = false)`). VisitController's @ModelAttribute("visit") loader takes an optional visitId. When visitId is present, the loader returns the visit the named pet already holds and must not add a new Visit to the pet. When visitId is absent, booking behaves as it does today. Pet gains a lookup by identity that returns null when absent, the same shape as Owner.getPet(Integer) (architecture-principles § Design Principles 2, consistency over novelty). GET and POST /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit reuse pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm. The form has no action attribute, so it posts back to the edit URL, and the heading already drops 'New' for a persisted visit. The narrowest reading leaves the template unchanged: a new button label would need keys in all eleven bundles (REQ-LANG-002), and no acceptance criterion asks for one. Showing the pet's visits, including the one being corrected, is acceptable. A successful POST redirects to /owners/{ownerId} with no flash message. A failed POST redisplays the form without saving. The non-future date rule is factored into one private check that both handlers call. This extends the controller deviation already recorded (system-design.md § Open Questions 2, architecture-principles § Pattern Catalog note) by a call site, not by a new rule. The Contracts rows for Pet, Visit, OwnerRepository and VisitController now cite REQ-VIS-003.
integration_points: Binding, correction POST: the bound object is the persisted Visit that the named pet already holds, behind an allow-list. A controller-level @InitBinder("visit") calls setAllowedFields("date", "description"), and the controller-wide id/*.id disallow stays in place (security-principles § Trust Boundaries, mass-assignment row). The correction handler takes the owner as @ModelAttribute(name = "owner", binding = false), so no request field binds onto Owner. system-design.md § Threat Model mass-assignment row records this.

Double, repository boundary: the existing VisitControllerTests fixture stubs OwnerRepository with @MockitoBean. That stub stays, a tolerated framework stub under testing-principles § Mocking Policy: @WebMvcTest excludes JPA, and a hand-written double of a Spring Data JpaRepository interface is out of proportion to the test. Stub findById so each call returns a freshly built owner-pet-visit graph, so that assertions never read an instance the request mutated. Assert 'no visit is added' on the owner passed to save (captured argument): the pet's visit count is unchanged, and the visit with the given id carries the new date and description. Assert 'the visit is unchanged' as save never being called.
Double, transport: MockMvc, the sanctioned web-layer harness (testing-principles § Mocking Policy; CLAUDE.md Testing Strategy).

Refusal, edge case 3: an unknown visitId, or a visit id held by a different pet, throws IllegalArgumentException from the loader. This is the same refusal edge case 1 uses for an unknown owner or pet. Scoping the lookup to the named pet's collection enforces ownership by construction. A MockMvc test observes the refusal as the thrown exception.

patterns.description: @ModelAttribute loader with an optional path variable chooses between a new entity and a persisted one
lookup by identity over an eagerly loaded collection, skipping new entities, returning null when absent; Pet's visit lookup takes the same shape
existing non-future date check with error code typeMismatch.visitDate; extract it once and call it from both handlers

risks.risk: The loader today always calls pet.addVisit(new Visit()). If the correction path keeps that call, the cascading save inserts a second, blank visit, which breaks 'no visit is added'.
risks.mitigation: Branch on visitId before constructing a Visit, following the PetController.findPet pattern. The capture assertion in the success test checks that the pet's visit count is unchanged (system-design.md § Contracts, Invariants paragraph).

risks.risk: Visit correction path: its cost scales with the owner's pets and the pet's visits (system-design.md § Scale and Load, row 'Visit booking and correction').
risks.mitigation: Use the simplest readable form, a linear scan over the eagerly loaded collections as Owner.getPet does. Sizes are unrecorded and treated as bounded.

risks.risk: Copying the non-future date check into the correction handler would create a second copy of a controller-held rule, which architecture-principles § Pattern Catalog counts against the Web controller row.
risks.mitigation: Keep one private check that both handlers call (system-design.md § Open Questions 2 records the call-site extension). Moving the rule into the domain stays an undecided human question and is out of scope for this slice.

risks.risk: If the correction POST binds request fields onto the Owner model attribute, other owner data could be changed through the correction route (mass assignment).
risks.mitigation: Use @ModelAttribute(name = "owner", binding = false) on the correction handler and allow-list the visit binder to date and description (security-principles § Trust Boundaries).

author: security-reviewer
recommendations: The owner binding=false and the visit allow-list are the only controls stopping mass assignment on the new POST route, and no test pins them. A test that posts extra owner or pet fields (e.g. firstName, a nested pets id) to the correction URL and asserts they are unchanged would catch a future removal.
approved_aspects: Ownership / IDOR: the correction resolves the visit only through the named owner and pet. VisitController.java:73 `Optional<Owner> optionalOwner = owners.findById(ownerId);`, :77 `Pet pet = owner.getPet(petId);`, then Pet.getVisit, which scans only this pet's persisted visits (`if (!visit.isNew() && Objects.equals(visit.getId(), id))`). A visitId that belongs to another pet or owner throws IllegalArgumentException before any bind or save. Each request loads the entities again rather than trusting an earlier request, per the security-principles 'Trusting cross-request state' row.

Mass assignment: the new `@InitBinder("visit")` sets `setAllowedFields("date", "description")` on top of the class-wide `setDisallowedFields("id", "*.id")`. The correction POST takes the owner as `@ModelAttribute(name = "owner", binding = false)`, so request parameters (including the form's hidden petId) cannot change owner or pet data. The allow-list also tightens the existing booking route, and no check was removed.

Validation: the correction handler has `@Valid Visit` (the @NotBlank description) and runs the same `rejectVisitDateNotInFuture` check as booking, returning the form before `owners.save` on any error. Spring Data's `findById` runs in its own transaction and open-in-view is off (per system-design), so the entity is detached and a refused edit's in-memory changes are not flushed. The only @Transactional in production code is on VetRepository (grep -rn -F '@Transactional' src/main/java).

Output escaping: createOrUpdateVisitForm.html renders visit and pet data with th:text only, and `grep -rn -F utext src/main/resources/templates` finds nothing. The form has no th:action, so it posts back to the URL it was loaded from.

Error disclosure: the new IllegalArgumentException message holds only integer path ids (visitId, petId, ownerId), matching the existing owner and pet messages. It carries no sensitive value to error.html, which renders `${message}` (error.html:18).

The new GET and POST /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit routes are unauthenticated and have no CSRF protection. That is the recorded demonstration baseline (security-principles.md 'What this application is'; system-design threat model 'Unauthenticated data modification' names visit edit routes), so it is not a finding. The change adds no query text, file, process, deserialization, or actuator surface.

No hardcoded secrets or dependency changes in the diff: build.gradle is not in `changeset.py --name-only`. Supply chain: dependencyCheckAnalyze is not configured (no match for grep -i dependencycheck in build.gradle), so no NVD match ran. The resolved runtime has Spring Boot plugin 4.1.1, spring-webmvc 7.0.9, and tools.jackson.core:jackson-databind 3.1.5 (./gradlew dependencies).

author: change-grader
summary: add correction of a booked visit's date and description

blast_radius.note: Two production files in the owner package (Pet.getVisit plus a new GET/POST edit route in VisitController), no sensitive paths, and a template reused unchanged. The only wider reach is that the shared @ModelAttribute loader and the new @InitBinder("visit") allow-list also run on the existing booking routes. Reading them shows the booking path still builds a new Visit, and the form's only visit fields are date and description, so booking behaves the same.

semantic_surprise.note: The code does what it says: the extracted rejectVisitDateNotInFuture has the same condition as the old inline check, lookup is limited to the named pet's persisted visits, and owner binding is off on the correction POST. The surprise is in the product behavior. A correction must pass the future-date rule, so a past visit can't keep its date. To fix a typo in last month's description, a user has to move the visit into the future, which falsifies clinical history. The PRD records this only as an open question. Smaller points: the reused template still labels the button 'Add Visit', and a refused correction redisplays the previous-visits table with the rejected values held in memory. Nothing is saved in that case.

test_adequacy.note: The tests check real outcomes. Recursive comparison of the saved owner graph proves the visit is updated in place and no visit is added. A tampering test posts owner fields and an id and asserts they are ignored. A parameterized refusal test covers a blank description, today, and a past date, each with never() save. A foreign-visit refusal test and four PetTests at the getVisit seam cover the rest. Remaining gap: persistence goes through a mocked repository, so the JPA merge-update is inferred from the existing cascade ALL mapping rather than exercised against a database.

reviewer_hedging.note: All four dispatched reviewers approved the final round with no findings or recommendations, and each aspect names its evidence. I checked the security reviewer's citations (VisitController.java:53, :58, :114, :138, :139) and the code-quality reviewer's system-design line 126, and they resolve. Round-1 caveats were fixed in the fix delta: a missing PetTests, a request to pin mass assignment in a test, and doc autofixes. The code-quality reviewer's round-1 suggestions (Optional, renaming loadPetWithVisit) were optional polish.

scope_deviation.note: The change delivers the requested GET/POST edit URL, reuses the template, adds no owner-page link and no cancellation, and records NG-5 narrowing in a new non-goal ADR as the owner asked. There were no build retries, no consultations, and no re-triage; the second design-block only applied doc autofixes. The one addition past the literal request is a new Scale and Load section in system-design, which is a design-doc record, not new behavior.

rationale: The change is small, contained, and well tested, and the reviewers approved cleanly with cited evidence. The decisive point is product behavior: the future-date rule means a past visit cannot be corrected without moving its date forward. Read processVisitCorrectionForm and the PRD open question, and decide whether to accept that before merging.
